raw:
You take the last bite of berry tart before a server removes your plate. The filling is sharp enough to cut through the sweetness, and the silver fork leaves a brief smear of dark juice on the china.

At the garden doors, Ashara pauses only long enough to look at Rashid.

“Twenty-eight minutes now.”

“You’re counting already?”

“You’re the one with another engagement.”

Rashid gives her a look that does not slow his stride. “Then stop spending them talking.”

They leave through the gardens toward the dueling grounds, the door settling shut behind them.

Aldric gathers his papers beneath one arm. “I’m due at evening office. After that, I have reading for tomorrow.”

Caelindra rises as well, though she angles toward the library rather than the front hall. “I intend to determine whether the assigned protocol text is as tedious as its title suggests.”

Seraphel folds her napkin neatly beside her cup, then picks up a slim notebook.

“I’ll sort my notes upstairs tonight;  
They’re ill arranged for morning light.”

She departs toward the stairs, gold catching softly at the edges of her hair.

Ysolde has already gone, leaving only her emptied glass and the small puddle of meltwater beneath it. Her remark about the clearing weather over the western bridge is the closest thing to a plan she offers.

Thessaly turns the spoon once more between her fingers. From the common room comes the dry, familiar riffle of cards being shuffled near the fire.

“A card game was mentioned,” she says. “I’m going to see whether its rules are tolerable before I agree to play.”

She sets the spoon down and heads through the open doorway. The common-room fire throws warm light across the floorboards; beyond it, the library lamps glow behind their glass shades, while the garden door still carries a breath of cold air from the plateau.

Within a few minutes, the formal dinner has become several separate evenings.
